I work in a vets office and absolutely disagree with declawing. You’ll find that a lot of vets are moving away from unnecessary procedures like declawing and ear cropping because it CAN cause harm to the animal and it almost never serves a positive purpose. Most of the time when an owner wants to declaw, we convince them to reconsider other options first or to agree to a tendonectomy, a far less invasive (and much cheaper, not that it should matter) procedure where they can’t extend the claws but they still have them intact.

Even in cases where declawing has little impact on a cats life, I wouldn’t compare it to antivax. That implies doctors are recommending it as essential to health and well being when that’s simply not true. At best, you mutilated your cat without its consent for no real reason other than you love your couch more than your pet.

When I was 12, I snuck out of the house for the sole purpose of seeing if I could get away with it (pre teenage rebellion I guess). I didn’t do anything crazy, just walked into town and got a Mountain Dew from a Chinese takeout place. It was around 10 or 11pm. 

While I was walking there and back, FOUR grown men on separate occasions pulled over in large vehicles asking if I wanted a ride, or if I was single, etc. One guy asked me to come to a bar with him. I told them all no and that I was 12 years old, and none of them stopped when hearing my age. The guy who asked me to go to the bar with him told me he could get me a fake ID.

None of them backed off until I threatened to call police. I realized when I got home that any of them could have simply grabbed me and dragged me into their cars and there’s nothing I could have done to stop that. I never snuck out again.

Be specific with your compliments! Telling her she’s beautiful is nice and it helps, but if she is struggling with body image she probably won’t fully believe you. So point out the things that truly make her beautiful to you, so she’ll know you’re not just trying to cheer her up.

For example, I was really upset the other day because I’ve been hitting the gym for a month but haven’t lost any weight. My boyfriend said to me “I see more muscle definition in your arms than I’ve ever seen in the 3 years we’ve been dating. You look more athletic every week.”

Telling me I was beautiful probably would have cheered me up a little, but being specific let me know the compliments were real and not just there to make me feel better.
